privacy.contact: Questions about your data, or want something deleted? Email aicryptoanalytics7@gmail.com.
privacy.cookies: We use two strictly necessary cookies: one to keep you logged in (HttpOnly, can't be read by JavaScript) and one for CSRF protection. Neither is used for tracking or advertising. There are no ads and no advertising trackers.
privacy.dataCollected: Username and a securely hashed password (we never store your plain-text password). Your email address, used for sign-up verification, password-reset codes, security notices and the weekly email if you turn it on. AI provider API keys you choose to connect, encrypted before storage. Your saved forecasts, schedules, portfolio analyses, price tips, community votes, in-app notifications, your public nickname if you set one and who invited you. For security, a log of sign-ins and other account events with the IP address and the browser or device used.
privacy.intro: This page explains what data AI Crypto Analytics collects, why, and how it's protected. AI Crypto Analytics is an independent project run by an individual developer.
privacy.rights: You can see, correct, export and delete your data: download everything in Settings → Your data, change your email anytime and delete the whole account in Settings. You can also object to processing or ask us to restrict it. If you think we handle your data unlawfully, you can complain to the Czech data protection authority (ÚOOÚ, www.uoou.cz) or the authority in your country.
privacy.thirdParty: Market data comes from public sources (CoinGecko, Alternative.me, Blockchair, DefiLlama, Hyperliquid, FRED, GDELT, news RSS feeds and Reddit); no personal data is sent to them. Emails are delivered through an email service provider. If you connect your own AI provider API key, your prompts (coin names, portfolio composition) are sent directly to that provider (Google, OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek or xAI) under its own privacy terms.

backtest.title: Statistical model backtest
backtest.help: Walk-forward test: for each past date the model only sees prices known on that day, forecasts ahead, and the result is compared with what actually happened.
backtest.intro: How well would the free statistical model have forecast in the past? For many historical dates the model forecasts using only the data available then, and the forecast is compared with the real price.
backtest.mapeHelp: Average percentage difference between the forecast price at the end of the horizon and the real price (MAPE). Lower is better.
backtest.naiveHelp: Benchmark: assume the price stays where it is today. If the model does not beat it, it has no edge in predicting price direction.
backtest.coverageHelp: How often the real price ended inside the uncertainty band. A well-calibrated model is close to 80%.
backtest.directionHelp: How often the model got the up/down direction right. 50% equals a coin flip.
backtest.chartLabel: Chart comparing forecast and actual prices in the backtest
backtest.verdictCalibrated: The uncertainty band is well calibrated: the real price was inside it in {value}% of cases (target 80%).
backtest.verdictNotCalibrated: The uncertainty band is not well calibrated: the real price was inside it in {value}% of cases (target 80%).
backtest.verdictBeatsNaive: The model had a lower error than the naive "price stays the same" forecast.
backtest.verdictNoEdge: The model's error is not clearly lower than the naive "price stays the same" forecast. Its value is in estimating the range (risk), not in predicting direction.
backtest.verdictDirection: Direction accuracy around 50% is normal for crypto: short-term price moves are largely random.

about.title: About the project
about.intro: AI Crypto Analytics is a web app for cryptocurrency analysis that combines forecasts from language models (AI) with a transparent statistical model and real market data. It focuses on honest accuracy evaluation, security and code quality.
about.feature.forecast: Price forecasts from several AI providers using the user's own API key, including a side-by-side model comparison chart.
about.feature.quant: A free statistical model with an 80% uncertainty band that works without an API key and backs up the AI when it fails.
about.feature.backtest: Walk-forward backtest of the model on historical data and automatic accuracy evaluation of saved forecasts.
about.feature.portfolio: Portfolio advisor with CSV import and risk analysis.
about.feature.market: Market sentiment: Fear & Greed index, news, on-chain whale activity and a macro events calendar (FOMC, CPI).
about.feature.security: Public share links for forecasts, an account activity log and alerts for sign-ins from new devices.
about.archAlt: Layer diagram: browser, API, services, external sources
about.arch.browser.name: Browser (React SPA on Netlify)
about.arch.browser.desc: User interface, charts, CSV processing locally in the browser.
about.arch.api.name: REST API (FastAPI on Render)
about.arch.api.desc: HttpOnly cookie authentication, CSRF protection, rate limiting, input validation.
about.arch.services.name: Application services and database
about.arch.services.desc: AI engine, statistical model, backtest, accuracy evaluation, audit log; PostgreSQL via SQLAlchemy.
about.arch.external.name: External services
about.arch.external.desc: Market data (CoinGecko, Blockchair, RSS) and AI provider APIs; responses are cached with fallbacks on outages.
about.source.coingecko: Live prices, historical charts, coin search.
about.source.news: Crypto news headlines for sentiment analysis.
about.source.macro: Official FOMC decision and CPI release dates.
about.quality: Backend and frontend are covered by automated tests (pytest, Vitest) and key user flows by Playwright end-to-end tests, all run by GitHub Actions on every push. Model accuracy is measured on real data and compared with a naive forecast.
about.security: Hashed passwords, encrypted user API keys, HttpOnly cookie sign-in with CSRF protection, optional 2FA, rate limiting, temporary lockout after failed attempts, security HTTP headers (CSP) and an account activity log.
about.author: Built by Martin Masaryk, a student developer from Prague.

privacy.purposesTitle: Why we use your data (legal basis)
privacy.purposes: To run your account and the features you use (performance of a contract). To keep the service secure, prevent abuse and send security alerts (legitimate interest). For the weekly email, morning briefing and waitlist only with your consent, which you can withdraw anytime. To keep billing records as required by law (legal obligation).
privacy.retention: Account data is kept until you delete your account; deleting it removes your data right away. Results of scored forecasts stay in the anonymous public statistics without any link to you, even after you delete a forecast or your account. The security log keeps only the most recent events.
terms.eligibility: You must be at least 18 years old. The app is an analytical tool: it does not hold money, trade or execute orders, and it is not a licensed investment service.
terms.withdrawal: If you are a consumer, you can withdraw from the subscription within 14 days of your first payment without giving a reason: email aicryptoanalytics7@gmail.com and we refund the full amount within 14 days, even though Premium already started at your request. Later payments can be stopped anytime by cancelling; they are not refunded for the period already started.
terms.law: These terms are governed by the laws of the Czech Republic; as a consumer you also keep the protection of the mandatory laws of your country. If we can't resolve a complaint together, you can turn to the Czech Trade Inspection Authority (www.coi.cz) for out-of-court dispute resolution.

privacy.pushData: If you turn on browser notifications, we store the delivery address your browser gives us (a link to your browser maker's push service — Google, Mozilla, Apple or Microsoft — and two encryption keys) and which kinds of notifications you want. The notification text is encrypted so only your browser can read it. Turning notifications off, signing out or deleting your account removes the address. Calendar reminders store the event you marked and are deleted two days after the event.
privacy.feedbackData: When you send feedback we store the message, its type, the page you were on, the app language and — if you are signed in — your account. Only the administrator reads it. If you delete your account, your messages stay but are no longer linked to you. Ask us by email to delete a message.

privacy.processors: To run the service we use: Netlify (website), Render (server and database), Cloudflare Turnstile (anti-bot check on sign-up, password reset and after repeated failed sign-ins; it processes your IP address and browser data), Brevo (sending emails), Sentry (error reports, if switched on) and, for browser notifications, the push service of your browser maker (Google, Mozilla, Apple or Microsoft), which only receives the encrypted notification. Some of these providers may process data in the USA; such transfers rely on the EU–US Data Privacy Framework or the European Commission's standard contractual clauses.
